---
title: "observe() and isolate() are no substitute for observeEvent()"
ref: SHY-06
categories: [Shiny]
impact: incoherent
attendu: "the action only runs when the button is clicked"
versions: "All versions of {shiny}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2019)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observe({
    input$save
    isolate({
      save_entry(name = input$name, amount = input$amount)
    })
  })
}
```
:::

This pitfall depends on a running Shiny app, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

An `observe()` runs once at startup, to discover its dependencies. Here, `save_entry()` is therefore called as soon as the app opens, before any click, with the default values of the fields.

The real dependency hangs on a lone `input$save` line, easy to delete by mistake during a cleanup. And if someone later adds an `input$...` outside the `isolate()`, the action also fires when that field changes.

## The remedy

`observeEvent()` states explicitly which event triggers the action, isolates the rest of the code, and by default ignores a button that was never clicked.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$save, {
    save_entry(name = input$name, amount = input$amount)
  })
}
```
:::
